bull.b: The substantial cash balance and extended runway reduce near-term financing pressure, giving Quantum-Si time to fund Proteus development, commercial preparation and manufacturing improvements before recurring revenue can scale.

Broad qualified interest across research institutions and biopharma supports a potentially meaningful customer base. Application opportunities such as AAV serotyping could expand platform adoption beyond initial proteomics workflows.

Lower operating costs should extend financial flexibility and reduce the expense burden required to commercialize the platform. Q2 OpEx also declined year over year, indicating that discipline is already emerging.

bear.b: The delay postpones customer evaluations, deployments and potential consumables pull-through. It also extends the period in which Quantum-Si must fund development without meaningful Proteus-driven recurring revenue.

A sharply declining and very small revenue base remains far below the company’s operating cost structure. Persistent losses and negative EBITDA indicate that commercial scale and sustainable cash generation have not yet been achieved.

Failure to regain minimum bid-price compliance by the applicable deadline could lead to delisting or corporate actions such as a reverse split. This creates an ongoing governance and market-access risk while commercialization remains delayed.
